candidates.exact_span: Regulations contained in 40 CFR §122.44 require that NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selecting the applicable enforceable limit for a parameter requires comparing technology-based ELG limits, water quality-based limits (numeric and/or narrative), and previous-permit limits; different readings of which comparator applies or how 'more stringent' is resolved would change the limit used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a limit is numeric versus narrative affects whether an ordinary reported measurement can be compared for compliance (Purpose A) and how missing or non-numeric results should be classified when no numeric comparison is applicable (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: Technology-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for TSS. Water quality-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for pH and TRC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This assigns the controlling limit type by parameter (TSS vs pH vs TRC); interpreting which basis governs each parameter changes which enforceable numeric limits are retrieved and compared to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44 (a) require technology-based effluent limitations to be placed in NPDES permits based on ELGs where applicable, on BPJ in the absence of guidelines, or on a combination of the two.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable technology-based limit for TSS depends on whether ELGs apply, BPJ applies, or a combination is used; different interpretations of applicability would change the derived numeric limit values.

candidates.exact_span: In the absence of promulgated guidelines for the discharge, permit conditions may be established using BPJ procedures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether promulgated ELGs exist for this discharge determines whether BPJ-derived limits govern; that choice can change the numeric technology-based limits applied to parameters such as TSS.

candidates.exact_span: BCT - Technology-based standard for the discharge from existing industrial point sources of conventional pollutants including BOD, TSS, fecal coliform, pH, and O&G.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classifying TSS (and pH) as conventional pollutants under BCT versus another technology level (BPT/BAT) affects which technology-based treatment standard and corresponding numeric limit basis applies.

candidates.exact_span: BAT - The most appropriate means available on a national basis for controlling the direct discharge of toxic and non-conventional pollutants to navigable waters.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TRC or other parameters are treated as toxic/non-conventional under BAT rather than conventional under BCT changes the technology-based standard and thus the enforceable numeric limit that could apply.

candidates.exact_span: It is proposed that the permit be reissued for a 5-year term following regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.46(a). This is a renewal of an existing permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Permit term and renewal status bear on which permit edition and conditions are in force during Federal FY2025 (monitoring obligations) and whether 'previous permit' limits remain a comparator when determining the more-stringent applicable discharge limit.

Limits and conditions are described as proposed rather than final; interpreting whether draft proposed limits are enforceable for FY2025 would change which numeric limits and monitoring requirements are treated as applicable.
